title: Existing CI Release Gate Dry-Run Binding
concrete_capability_transition: Brownie release engineering binds the repository-local release gate dry-run into the existing GitHub-CI-invoked VSIX check path without editing workflow files, making release-gate plan drift a guarded CI failure while Runtime Release Ready remains false.

strategic_capability_mapping.transition: The existing CI path now executes the release gate dry-run through brownie-vsix check and guard engines fail closed if that binding is removed.
strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: This advances runtime-release-guard-ci through an owner-approved equivalent path while workflow-scope credentials remain absent; it does not claim direct workflow hardening or Runtime Release Ready.

answers.strategic_capabilities: The phase advances headless_autonomous_development by making the mandatory release gate plan visible and guarded in the existing CI-invoked VSIX check path.
answers.new_capability: A contributor or CI run that executes pnpm --filter brownie-vsix check now also executes pnpm --workspace-root release:gate -- --dry-run, and guards reject removing that binding.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before this phase, CI checked the release contract and many release guards but did not directly exercise the release gate plan from the CI-invoked path, so release:gate command-list drift could escape the mandatory VSIX check.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie would retain a local release gate whose command plan could diverge from the CI-required check path until workflow-scope credentials are available.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase does not add another release contract, workflow edit, or ledger/platform feature; it binds the existing release gate dry-run into the existing CI path and guards that binding.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. No JSON-RPC method or Runtime protocol surface is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The dry-run output is existing release-gate evidence, not a new user-facing summary or Runtime diagnostic endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Build/release behavior changes: brownie-vsix check now includes the release gate dry-run, and release/readiness guards fail closed if the CI-invoked path omits it.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The autonomous release loop can continue using existing CI while workflow-scope credentials are unavailable, with less room for local release-gate drift.
answers.milestone_progress: RRP-8.6 narrows runtime-release-guard-ci by closing the permitted existing-CI dry-run binding slice while preserving release-blocking workflow, artifact, audit, governance, and owner-decision evidence.

closed_debt: runtime-release-guard-ci existing-CI release gate dry-run binding
non_goals: hosted services, scheduler, durable queue, supervisor, SaaS, RBAC, Vault, BDK, or Enterprise admin

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or removes release-blocking artifact, audit, governance, workflow, review, or owner-setting evidence
pnpm --filter brownie-vsix check does not invoke pnpm --workspace-root release:gate -- --dry-run
guard:release-contract or guard:runtime-release-readiness does not fail closed when the VSIX check path omits the release gate dry-run
workflow files are modified without workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent path
license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or signing infrastructure are changed by Runtime automation

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-8.6 changes CI-invoked package scripts and release/readiness guard engines. Review must confirm the existing VSIX check path invokes release:gate -- --dry-run, guards fail closed if it is removed, no .github workflow files were edited, and runtime_release_ready remains false.

exit_criteria: scripts/guard-release-contract.mjs rejects VSIX check paths that omit the release gate dry-run.
scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.mjs rejects VSIX check paths that omit the release gate dry-run.
pnpm --workspace-root release:gate -- --dry-run passes and lists the mandatory release gate command plan.
pnpm --filter brownie-vsix check passes with runtime_release_ready=false and release_ready=false.

accepted_capability: The existing CI-invoked VSIX check path exercises the release gate dry-run.
Release and readiness guards keep that dry-run binding mandatory.
Direct workflow hardening remains blocked by missing workflow-scope credentials.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until release evidence and owner-controlled settings are complete.
behavior_evidence: node --test scripts/guard-release-contract.test.mjs validates fail-closed release gate dry-run binding checks.
node --test scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.test.mjs validates fail-closed existing CI path coverage.
pnpm --workspace-root guard:release-contract validates the live Runtime release contract and VSIX check binding.
pnpm --workspace-root guard:runtime-release-readiness validates the live audit and VSIX check binding.
pnpm --workspace-root release:gate -- --dry-run emits the mandatory release gate command plan.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
GitHub workflow settings, branch protection, protected tags, signing authority, license choice, and publish posture remain owner-controlled until explicitly provided.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not generate or publish release tags, packages, license metadata, signatures, or release assets.

Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, durable queue, supervisor, SaaS control plane, customer RBAC, Vault, billing, BDK, Enterprise admin, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or remote Git capability expansion.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected editing .github/workflows/ci.yml because active GitHub credentials still lack workflow scope.
Rejected claiming runtime-release-guard-ci closed because release artifacts, audits, provenance, governance, and owner decisions remain incomplete.
Rejected a docs-only update because the existing CI-invoked check path must execute and guard the release gate dry-run.
technical_debt: runtime-release-guard-ci remains open until actual vulnerability/license audit execution, cross-platform artifacts, artifact smoke tests, direct workflow enforcement or stronger owner-approved CI enforcement, provenance, signing/integrity, branch protection/status checks, independent reviews, and owner settings are complete.
Owner license, publish posture, signing or integrity mechanism, branch protection, protected tags, and independent reviews remain required before Runtime Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Continue with the next bounded runtime-release-guard-ci slice that can be completed without workflow scope or owner-only settings, or wait for workflow-scope credentials for direct workflow hardening.

runtime_release_dod: Closed RRP-1 through RRP-7.2 and RRP-5.18 evidence remains in force and is not reimplemented.
RRP-8.6 binds the local release gate dry-run into existing CI evidence without treating it as final Release Ready.
Missing release artifacts, scans, SBOM, checksums, signatures or integrity proof, provenance, workflow run enforcement, tested commit, and independent reviews remain release-blocking.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, durable queues, worker leases, hosted isolation, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside local Runtime v0.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside this phase.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging publication, license choice, signing authority, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain owner-controlled or later release work.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-8.6.

technical_debt.next_action: Add actual vulnerability/license audits, cross-platform artifacts and smoke tests, governance evidence, and direct workflow or stronger owner-approved CI enforcement before Runtime Release Ready.
Owner must provide workflow-scope credentials for direct .github workflow gate closure.
Owner must choose license and publish posture before public OSS release; Runtime automation must not change license, publish metadata, release tags, or release assets.

closeout_review.evidence: RRP-8.6 binds release:gate dry-run into the existing CI-invoked VSIX check path and guards that binding, while workflow enforcement and release evidence remain incomplete.
